analysis.title: GS Prime - Hedge Fund updates: Asia Managers sustain -6.8% MTD drawdown; selling in AI exposure accelerates
key_insights: Asia Fundamental L/S managers lost 2.6% in a day. Month-to-date drawdown is -6.8%, and YTD returns of 16.7% are back to July lows, about 23% below a ~40% high in late June.
Beta and asset selection alpha were the main drivers of the Asia MTD drawdown, followed by volatility, Info Tech and Korea tilts.
Global Fundamental L/S managers were down 0.5% on the day and are +10% YTD. Global Systematic L/S managers were down 1.4% on the day and are +20% YTD.
The Global Prime book had large net selling (-2.1 SD) as risk unwinds led, with long sales exceeding short sales.
Asian equities saw net selling of -1.0 SD led by Korea and Taiwan. Long sales exceeded short covers 3 to 1, and other major markets were roughly flat on a net basis.
Selling in Korea and Taiwan was dominated by long unwinds in AI-related names. The region is moderately net sold week over week and month to date in October.
Korea net allocations fell 75 bps MTD to 3.64% (32nd percentile 1-year, 86th percentile 5-year). Gross allocation is 2.59% (41st percentile 1-year, 88th percentile 5-year).
Taiwan was less affected because of net buying in the first week of October. Gross allocation is near all-time highs at 3.96% (94th percentile 1-year, 99th percentile 5-year).
risk_factors: Accelerating AI sell-off is driving long unwinds across Asia hedge fund books.
Taiwan gross exposure sits near record levels, leaving room for further de-risking if the AI selling continues.
